passage: Every morning at the bus stop in Buenos Aires, Layla's tongue turned to cardboard when Diego walked up. Her brain ran the film in advance: she says something odd, he raises an eyebrow, the whole bus laughs. So she stared at her phone and said nothing. On Thursday her friend Sofia muttered, "Just ask him about the maths quiz. People talk about the quiz." Layla's palms were damp, but when Diego stopped next to her she blurted, "Did you finish question six?" Her voice cracked on six. Diego laughed, not unkindly. "No, I gave up. Did you?" They spent the ride complaining about question six. She got off at her stop still red in the face, but she noticed she was smiling, and nobody on the bus had cared at all.

qa.q: Where did Layla see Diego every morning?
qa.a: She saw him at the bus stop in Buenos Aires.

qa.q: Why did Layla stare at her phone instead of speaking?
qa.a: She was afraid of embarrassing herself. Her mind ran the film in advance of saying something odd and the whole bus laughing.

qa.q: What small step helped Layla break the silence?
qa.a: She began with ordinary talk by asking about question six of the maths quiz, as her friend Sofia suggested, and accepted that her voice cracking was okay.

qa.q: How might Diego have seen her question?
qa.a: Probably as a friendly, normal thing to say. He laughed but not unkindly, and he joined in complaining about the question. 😊

grounding: Layla freezes near her crush and imagines embarrassment, then starts with ordinary friendly talk and finds awkwardness is normal.

passage:
Eshaan, you keep hiding when that girl from your tuition walks past. Sit. I was exactly the same.
In Class 9 in Lucknow, there was Shabnam, who sat by the window. Whenever she came near, my tongue turned to wood. I'd lie in bed imagining every way I might embarrass myself: dropping my books, saying something stupid, my voice cracking.
My plan was to write her a long, dramatic letter and give it to her on the last day of school. Thank God I never did.
The turning point was a pencil. One day hers broke in the exam hall, and before I could think, I held mine out. She said, "Thanks, Raghav," and smiled.
The next day I said, "Did the pencil survive?" It was a ridiculous line. She laughed anyway.
After that we talked about ordinary things: exams, cricket, rain. Awkward, yes, but that's normal. Start with a pencil, beta.

qa.q: How did young Raghav feel whenever Shabnam came near?
qa.a: He felt shy and frozen, his tongue turning to wood, and anxious about all the ways he might embarrass himself.

qa.q: What was the turning point in young Raghav's story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Offering his pencil when hers broke led to ordinary, friendly talk, which was far better than hiding or a dramatic letter.

qa.q: How might Shabnam have seen young Raghav at first?
qa.a: She probably saw a quiet boy who never spoke, so the pencil and silly joke showed her a friendly side of him.

grounding: An elder recalls freezing near a crush and starting with ordinary friendly talk instead of hiding or a dramatic letter.

passage:
Mehak had been imagining the moment for months. Now it was happening in the worst possible way: a sudden downpour, one tiny bus shelter, and Aman from the science club squeezed right next to her, both of them soaked.
Her mind raced. Say something smart. No, you'll stutter. Your hair looks like a wet mop. He'll think you're weird.
She stared at the rain and said nothing for five whole minutes.
Her phone buzzed. Lavanya, her best friend: "Is that AMAN next to u?? just say hi. normal hi."
Mehak took a breath. "The bus is always late when it rains," she said. Her voice came out a little squeaky.
Aman grinned. "Always. Once I waited an hour and missed my own birthday cake."
Mehak laughed, the awkwardness still there but smaller. By the time the bus came, they'd talked about the science fair, and she hadn't died of embarrassment even once.

qa.q: Where were Mehak and Aman stuck during the downpour?
What was Mehak worried about while standing next to Aman?
qa.a: She felt nervous and embarrassed, imagining she would stutter, look messy with wet hair and seem weird.

qa.q: What small step helped Mehak, and why?
qa.a: Following Lavanya's advice to say a normal hi, she made ordinary talk about the late bus, which eased the awkwardness.

qa.q: How might Aman see the moment at the bus stop?
qa.a: Aman seems relaxed and happy to chat, even sharing a funny story, probably not noticing how nervous Mehak felt.

grounding: A shy teen freezes near her crush but starts with ordinary, friendly talk and accepts that awkwardness is normal.
